items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: the one who said that Bix died of everything

ctx.x: too wonderful wit he had and the sense of always I mean he could think of the clever things to say he was
the one who said that Bix died of everything which I think was a very good way of putting it when they asked when they were trying to figure out how he died and he said he died of everything

he could think up things that you know like other people on the way home they said I wish I'd said that but he always had everything ready very sharp tongue too in some ways it made a few people mad at times he's always trying to ride Mez in the late years he evidently didn't get along too well with him so he was always trying to belittle him but anyway to get back to Panassier Mez of course was one of his big favorites after Jimmy Noon I think he thought Mez was about the greatest clarinetist that had ever lived…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: Vicks was another, really a beautiful vocal, mellow tone

ctx.x: So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…
Well, of course, we'll never know what Joe Oliver really sounded like.
